title: All-Inclusive in Primošten 2027: Hotel Zora, Prices, Options
metaDescription: Primošten has one all-inclusive option: Hotel Zora. See 2027 per-person prices vs half-board and apartments, plus who it suits and nearby alternatives.
content:
## Does Primošten Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Primošten has no large all-inclusive resort in the Turkish or Spanish style. It has one classic hotel complex, **Hotel Zora**, on the Raduča peninsula next to the old town. The hotel has 324 rooms in nine buildings, rated 3* (Comfort) and 4* (Premier Club). Croatian tour operators currently sell it on half-board and on an **"All Inclusive Light"** basis for the 2026 season. A few small apartment houses also advertise an "all-inclusive" label, but this usually means a stocked self-catering unit, not meals and drinks.

The label matters. At Zora, "all inclusive light" is a step above half-board, not an unlimited-everything wristband. The terms differ by operator, so check them before paying.

## What Is Typically Included

Croatian "All Inclusive Light" packages usually cover:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner as a buffet
- Local house drinks with meals and during set hours
- Use of the hotel pool and beach area
- Kids club and playground access
- Free Wi-Fi

Extras are normally charged on top. Parking costs about €6 per day, and a room fridge about €10 per stay. Tourist tax is €1.80 per adult per night and €0.90 for ages 12–17. Children under 12 are exempt only where the local rules say so, so confirm at booking.

## All-Inclusive Prices in Primošten: Peak vs Shoulder Season

All prices are per person per night, based on 2026 agency rates for a Comfort balcony room. Use them as a guide for 2027.

| Board type | Shoulder (Sept–Oct) | Peak (July–August) |
|---|---|---|
| All Inclusive Light | €71–96 | €128–135 |
| Half-board plus | about €60–76 | about €100–115 |
| Private apartment, self-catering | about €30–45 | about €50–75 |

The all-inclusive step costs about €15–25 per person per night more than half-board. Premier and sea-side suites run higher, up to about €297 per person in peak weeks. Children under 7 often stay free on an extra bed. Ages 7–12 usually pay a reduced rate of roughly €30–65 per night, depending on the offer.

Apartment costs are a rough estimate for two adults sharing a one-bedroom unit at about €60–150 per night, before groceries and eating out. A couple eating out daily in Primošten will spend about €50–70 per day on meals and drinks. That brings an apartment holiday close to Zora's half-board price.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits in Primošten

**It works well for:**

- **Families with children under 7.** Free or discounted places, a kids club and a pool remove most daily decisions.
- **Short stays of 3–5 nights.** Shopping and cooking for a four-night trip is not worth the effort.
- **Early-September and October trips.** Rates fall to the €71–96 range and the beach is quieter.
- **Guests who want to drink at meals** without checking a bill.

**Self-catering is better for:**

- **Stays of 7 nights or more.** Daily buffets get repetitive.
- **Couples and groups who like konobas.** Primošten's old-town restaurants and the Rogoznica coast are a main reason to visit.
- **Peak-season travellers on a budget.** At €128–135 per person, a family of four pays over €500 per night.
- **Anyone who wants to be out by 9 a.m.** Meal-time limits waste the day.

All-inclusive in Primošten is a poor deal for people who plan to eat out and see the coast. In a town this small, the best food is the main reason to leave the hotel, and you would be paying for buffets you skip.

## Nearest Places With All-Inclusive

Primošten itself offers only the Zora option. For a wider choice, look at these towns:

- **Vodice** (about 22 km north, 25 minutes by car). It has the most resort-style hotels nearby, including Matilde Beach Resort and Hotel Olympia Sky, and many listings offer board options.
- **Šibenik and Solaris** (about 28–30 km). The Amadria Park complex has family hotels with pools and kids pools, and D-Resort Šibenik is also in the area. Check the board basis on each date, because it varies.
- **Trogir and the Čiovo area** (about 27 km south). Several hotels and villas list all-inclusive on booking platforms.

Vodice and Šibenik hotels are mostly half-board or breakfast, with all-inclusive on selected dates. Vodice resorts start at roughly €80–90 per person per night.

## Local Tips

- Book Zora through a Croatian agency package, not directly. Agencies often include a free child place and "all inclusive light" at lower rates.
- Mid-September (about 10–19 Sept) is the best value week. Rates are near €81 per person with the sea still warm.
- Ask whether drinks are served at the bar or only at meals. This is the biggest difference between "light" and full all-inclusive.
- The walk from Zora to the old town takes about 10 minutes, so a rental car is not needed.
- Pair a half-board stay with a lunch in town. This is cheaper than all-inclusive and gives you both buffet and konoba.

## FAQ

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive resort in Primošten?
faq.answer: There is no full resort of the Mediterranean type. Hotel Zora, a 324-room hotel on the Raduča peninsula, sells an "All Inclusive Light" board through Croatian travel agencies. It is the only classic hotel in the town.

faq.question: How much is all-inclusive per person per night in Primošten?
faq.answer: At Hotel Zora, All Inclusive Light costs about €71–96 per person per night in shoulder season and about €128–135 in peak summer for a Comfort balcony room. Children under 7 often stay free on an extra bed.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Primošten?
faq.answer: No. All Inclusive Light costs about €15–25 more per person per night than half-board at Zora. It pays off only if you use the lunch and drink inclusions.

faq.question: Is an apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Primošten?
faq.answer: Usually yes for two or more adults staying a week. A private apartment is roughly €30–75 per person per night, but food and drinks are extra, so the gap narrows if you eat out daily.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive hotel to Primošten?
faq.answer: Vodice is closest, about 22 km away, with several resort hotels. Šibenik and Solaris (about 28–30 km) and the Trogir area (about 27 km) also have options. Board types vary by date, so check before booking.

quickAnswer: Primošten has no true all-inclusive resort, but Hotel Zora, a 324-room 3/4-star complex on the Raduča peninsula, sells an "All Inclusive Light" board through Croatian agencies. Expect roughly €71–96 per person per night in shoulder season and €128–135 in peak. It suits families with small children on short stays.
